title: The price as instruction
body: A price computed for one buyer from their data, rather than posted for everyone — the same number, carrying the seller's model of you instead of the market's signal. Extends Gardiner Means's “administered prices” (1930s) from the boardroom to the shopper.
foot: proposed 3 Oct · prior art checked 3 Oct · none found · one recent counter-argument
artTitle: Software is changing what a price is

title: Sensory syncrasis
body: The whole configuration of how the brain blends its senses: how much it trusts each one, how loud it turns them all, whether it fuses or separates them, the balance between body and world, and how long a setting lasts. From the Greek root of idiosyncrasy.
foot: proposed 4 Oct · web check 4 Oct: the word names only a wasp genus (Wikispecies); no use in perception · scholarly check pending

title: Typomora
body: The typed delay in McLuhan's predicted return to voice: fifty years in which the keyboard, not the medium, kept networked communication typographic. Typos, type, and mora, delay — also the unit of spoken time.
foot: proposed 4 Oct · web check 4 Oct: no use found · scholarly check pending

title: Epanaphony
body: The return of voice as the way we put language into machines — dictation, voice notes, talking to AI — that closes the typomora. Oral in production, typographic in storage.
foot: proposed 4 Oct · web check 4 Oct: no use found; nearest is epanaphora · scholarly check pending

title: Narcocrasis
body: In drug dependence, the part a person stops noticing is not the drug but their own shifted baseline: flatter pleasures, a restless body, a raised stress tone. The drug feels like the fix; the changed baseline feels like how the world is.
foot: coined 5 Oct in Narcocrasis · name check pending

title: Anacrasis
body: Recovery as re-setting that baseline, not only removing the drug. The ancient Greek word anakrasis meant mixing with others, and the evidence points the same way: what helps the reset last is other people.
foot: from Narcocrasis · ancient Greek, reused 5 Oct · name check pending

title: Pharmakrasis
body: Every class of drug sets its own characteristic balance of the senses: cannabis speeds felt time, ketamine loosens the sense of owning a body, LSD deepens the response to music. A drug, on this view, is a technology of the senses, like a medium but more direct.
foot: coined 5 Oct in Pharmakrasis · name check pending

title: Heterocrasis
body: People start from different balances of the senses before any medium touches them. ADHD may be one such starting point, most clearly in how loudly the brain turns all its signals up or down.
foot: coined 5 Oct in Heterocrasis · name check pending

title: Exocrasis
body: Part of how we sense and remember now lives outside the body, in keyboards, search, saved files and the network. The computing environment holds some of the balance the brain used to hold.
foot: coined 5 Oct in Exocrasis · name check pending

title: The visual detour
body: The internet from about 1990 to 2022 as a fifty-year swing back toward print — screens of text and keyboards — inside the longer return to speech that McLuhan predicted, now ending as voice interfaces take over.
